### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c5a988aca3958c9f1486f80b922e4d8565fd491b` — the merge of head `5a6e8fad3087ae745d71794bc9bc28db0b3153bb` into base `8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c5a988aca3958c9f1486f80b922e4d8565fd491b && git checkout c5a988aca3958c9f1486f80b922e4d8565fd491b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8 5a6e8fad3087ae745d71794bc9bc28db0b3153bb && git checkout -B drift-repro 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8 && git merge --no-ff 5a6e8fad3087ae745d71794bc9bc28db0b3153bb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8ae0ab9b0d77d56473e89dae9fe437778172dda8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `22db7aee6047702085db7002930a061ef55a421d`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md + packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts (`fieldPatchTargetMisses`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`patchedField`, `applyFieldPatches`), skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json (cases 5 and 7), scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs (the `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` row, 6078), HotCRM `main` 6961ab1 src/sales/objects/account.object.ts and src/sales/objects/contact.object.ts

Inputs read: card #30944 (body, the triage comment and the claim comment), PR #30995 (body, 6-file list, net diff against merge base `acd190b22`), the head's 42 check-runs, HotCRM `origin/main` at `6961ab1`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldPatches`, `fieldPatchesDescription()`: description text only. The added sentence ("An option of a field bound to a shared `picklist` is never patchable … only a field declaring its own `options` takes an option patch") and the new example change the published description, which is emitted into the JSON Schema and into `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx`. No `z.` shape, key, alias, refusal or default changes, so **the accept set is unchanged. Right.**
- `ObjectExtensionSchema` TSDoc `@example`: this changes a comment that ships in the `.d.ts`. No type changes. **Right.**
- `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: changes the taught example and deletes one clause. This is published through `@objectstack/skills`, and it has no API surface. **Right.**
- What the change claims about runtime matches the code. `fieldPatchTargetMisses` pushes `picklist-option` for every `options` key of a field with a non-empty `picklist`, before it looks at values (L112–126). A field without a picklist and with no inline options gets an `option` miss that says its values are "none" (L128–139), so "only a field declaring its own `options` takes an option patch" holds. `patchedField` skips `options` when `picklistBound` (registry.ts L650–651). "Its labels are the picklist's" matches the judge's own message and the `finishServedObject` docblock. **Right.**
- No code in `metadata-core` or `objectql` is touched. The regenerated reference row matches the new description text exactly, and `check:docs` runs in `Type Check · source gates`, which concluded **success**.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/skills': patch`: the diff publishes changed teaching text only. **Matches.**
- `'@objectstack/spec': patch`: the diff publishes changed description and TSDoc text only, with no schema or type change. **Matches.** Both packages are in the `fixed` group of `.changeset/config.json`. Neither changeset is a `skip-changeset`.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear in both changesets and in the PR body, and both are **correct**. No authorable key or accepted value is added or removed, and the protocol is not touched.
- The skills changeset's prose does not match the tree (should-fix S1 below). It says "the sentence before it names `industry` as the picklist-bound field whose options no patch reaches". The sentence on the head (SKILL.md L363) says only "a `picklist`-bound field's options are never patchable" and does not name `industry`. This prose lands in the CHANGELOG. The level is unaffected.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier waiver** ("developed below that tier; the dispatching seat runs the contract review"): answered. This record is served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, and the face is schema plus a governed path (`--paths` gives both `hits`).
- **Out of scope, `options` shape error message near object.zod.ts L5034** (`options: { technology: { label: 'Tech' } }`): I concur that it stays. It shows the map-versus-list shape inside a refusal message and names no target field, so it is not a HotCRM patch an author copies.
- **Ratchet payment "by the seat's ruling"**: judged in ④. It holds.
- **Local heap note** (`check:test-typecheck` at 4096 MB) and **`check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test` exit 3 on a shallow clone**: both come from the dev's container, not from the tree. CI is the verdict. Of the type-check jobs, `Type Check · workspace`, `· consumer gates` and `· debt ledger` are still **in progress** on this head.
- **Serial constraint with PR #30947** (same SKILL.md): resolved. #30947 merged at 2026-11-06T15:26Z, its merge commit is an ancestor of this head, and SKILL.md on `origin/main` equals the merge base.
- **Check-runs on the head** (42 in total): 14 completed **success** (`Type Check · source gates`, which carries the token ratchet and `check:docs`; `Spec property liveness`; `Lint · ESLint`; `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`; `Check Changeset`; `Governed Surface Queue Guard`; `PR-body guards`; `Check Documentation Links`; `Dogfood Regression Gate`; `Check PR Size`; `Flag docs affected by code changes`; `Plan Test Core shards`; `Auto Label`; `filter`). 7 were skipped (opt-in or path-filtered). 21 are **in progress**: `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Test Core (1–8/8)`, `Live E2E UI`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check · consumer gates` (carries `check:skill-examples`), `Type Check · debt ledger`, `Lint · docs & code guards` (carries `check:skill-identifier-liveness`), `Lint · repo & tooling gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests`, `Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus`, `Lint · scoped · query-options erasure`. None has failed. This PASS does not stand in for them: the merge waits on every check being green.

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: holds.**
- I copied the new example verbatim, `defineObjectExtension({ extend: 'crm_account', fieldPatches: { industry: { label: 'Sector' }, type: { options: { customer: { label: 'Client' } } } } })`, and checked it against HotCRM `main` `6961ab1`. `industry` is declared at L311–318 (`Field.select({ label: 'Industry', group: 'basic', picklist: 'industry' })`), so `fieldOf` finds it, and the patch has no `options`, so it raises no miss. `type` is declared at L300–309 with inline `options` and no `picklist`, and L305 is `{ label: 'Customer', value: 'customer', … }`. `customer` is therefore a stored value, `values.includes('customer')` is true, and it raises no miss. `fieldPatchTargetMisses` returns `[]`. `patchedField` applies `label` to `industry` and relabels `type`'s `customer` option. The copy passes the install door, `os validate` and the fold.
- The card's constraint holds. `extend: 'crm_account'` and `label: 'Sector'` are whole tokens on L364, as eval case 5 (`must_contain` `extend: 'crm_account'`) and case 7 (`extend: 'crm_account'`, `fieldPatches`, `label: 'Sector'`) need. The example no longer contradicts the rule stated just before it ("a `picklist`-bound field's options are never patchable"), and it agrees with case 7's expected output ("no `options` entry belongs on this patch").
- **Ratchet payment: no fact is lost.** The deleted clause was "; a base field changes only through `fieldPatches`", which closed the `.custom` paragraph. It carries three facts, and each survives in the same file:
  - (a) A base field can be changed, and the channel is `fieldPatches`. L355: "**Relabel a field the owner declares with `fieldPatches`**".
  - (b) The change is display-only. L356–360: the whitelist keys only, "the type, values and rules stay the owner's".
  - (c) No other channel exists (the "only"). `fields` is closed by L355–357 ("never by redeclaring it in `fields`"), and in a `.custom` extension it is a hard refusal through L370–371: a base field is unsuffixed, because `__c` is reserved to the pair, and "an unsuffixed field in a `.custom` extension, is refused". `overrides` is closed by L368 ("it takes no `overrides` declaration"). Removal is closed by L349 ("can add but never remove").

  Eval case 5's expected-output sentence ("A change to one of HotCRM's own fields goes through `fieldPatches` (display properties only)") is carried by (a) and (b), and it is not a `must_contain` token. The clause was a restatement, so the deletion is a real payment and no rule is lost.
- Token count: the head blob is 24291 bytes. Minus the 20-byte stamp line, ceil(24271/4) = **6068**, against the row's ceiling of **6078**. The base was 24331 bytes, which counts to 6078. The example costs 10 bytes and the payment frees 50, a net of −40 bytes. No row moves and no re-wrap is involved. The ratchet runs in `Type Check · source gates`, which concluded success. The 10-token headroom could be returned by lowering the row. The script says this is encouraged but optional, so it is not a finding.
- **S1 (should-fix)**: make the tree and the skills changeset agree. The changeset says the sentence before the example names `industry` as the picklist-bound field, but it does not. As things stand, the example patches `type`'s options and not `industry`'s without saying why, so the reader learns the rule but not which HotCRM field it applies to. Case 7 expects the agent to know "HotCRM's `industry` takes its options from the `industry` picklist". There are two fixes. One is a few words on L363, e.g. "(HotCRM's `industry` is)", which fits in the 10-token headroom. The other is to drop the claim from the changeset.

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: holds.**
- The new description sentence is true of the code it cites (see ①). I copied the new description example verbatim, `fieldPatches: { industry: { label: 'Sector', inlineHelpText: 'The market the account sells into' }, type: { options: { customer: { label: 'Client' } } } }`, under `extend: 'crm_account'`. `inlineHelpText` is a whitelisted field key, and the rest goes through the same path as the skill example, so it passes `fieldPatchTargetMisses` on HotCRM `main` with `[]`. The rule is stated next to the example, as the card's Expected asks.
- **S2 (should-fix)**: the TSDoc `@example` targets `extend: 'contact'`, and its new comment states "`industry` is picklist-bound, so only its label; `type` declares its own options". Those are facts about HotCRM's `crm_account`, not about any `contact`. HotCRM's `crm_contact` declares neither `industry` nor `type`, so a copy against it gets two `field` misses. Patching `industry` on `contact` predates this PR, and the block is plainly illustrative (`Field.select([...])`), so this does not refuse a copy on the card's scenario. But the comment the PR adds now asserts the shape of a target it does not name. Either word the comment as a condition ("where `industry` is picklist-bound, as on HotCRM's `crm_account`") or split the `fieldPatches` line out under an account target.

No must-fix. Both should-fixes are text-only and do not block this head.

## Contract review

Scope: packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts, skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md + packages/spec/src/data/field-customization.ts (`BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST`), packages/metadata-core/src/extension-field-patch-targets.ts (`fieldPatchTargetMisses`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`patchedField`, `applyFieldPatches`), skills/objectstack-data/evals/objects-fields-relationships.json (cases 5 and 7), scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs (the `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md` row, 6078), HotCRM `main` 6961ab1 src/sales/objects/account.object.ts and src/sales/objects/contact.object.ts

This is a delta review against the PASS recorded on `22db7aee`. The delta is one commit, `7c661dec1`, whose parent is `22db7aee`. It changes two files: `.changeset/30944-skills-field-patches-example-hotcrm.md` (one line) and `packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts` (the TSDoc `@example` comment, which goes from one line to two). The net diff against it is the same six files as before. `SKILL.md`, both docs pages, the spec changeset and `fieldPatchesDescription()` are byte-identical to `22db7aee`.

### ① Derived judgments

- `ObjectExtensionSchema.fieldPatches`, `fieldPatchesDescription()`: unchanged since `22db7aee`. The text is description-only and the accept set is unchanged. The sentence on picklist-bound options is true of `fieldPatchTargetMisses` (L112–126) and `patchedField` (registry.ts L650–651). **Right.**
- `ObjectExtensionSchema` TSDoc `@example`: a comment only, shipped in the `.d.ts`. No type changes. **Right as a surface change.** Its new wording is **false**, though: see M1 in ④.
- `skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: unchanged since `22db7aee`. It is teaching text published through `@objectstack/skills` and has no API surface. **Right.**
- The regenerated `content/docs/references/data/object.mdx` row still matches the description, because the delta does not touch the description. `check:docs` runs in `Type Check · source gates`, which concluded **success** on this head.

### ② Semver level

- `'@objectstack/skills': patch` and `'@objectstack/spec': patch`: the diff publishes teaching text, description text and TSDoc only. **Both match.** Both packages are in the changeset config's `fixed` group, and neither changeset is a `skip-changeset`.
- `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none` appear in both changesets and in the PR body, and both are **correct**.
- **S1 from `22db7aee` is resolved and true.** The skills changeset no longer says the sentence before the example names `industry`. What it still says now matches the tree: the example sets `industry`'s `label` only and patches `type`'s `customer` option, and the deleted `.custom` clause is a restatement (see ④). The skill text was left unchanged, which was one of the two ways to resolve S1.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier waiver**: answered. This record is served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, on the schema face plus a governed path.
- **Out of scope, `options` shape error message near object.zod.ts L5034**: I still concur that it stays. It illustrates the map shape and names no target field.

- **Serial constraint with PR #30947**: resolved. It merged, and its merge commit is an ancestor of this head.
- **Check-runs on `7c661dec`** (67 in total):
  - **55 completed success.** These include every Type Check job (`source gates`, `workspace`, `consumer gates` with `check:skill-examples`, `debt ledger`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check UI`), every Lint job (`docs & code guards` with `check:skill-identifier-liveness`, `repo & tooling gates`, `CI, release & engine gates`, the three `scoped` jobs, `ESLint`, `PM dispatch-gates`, `Lint & Repo Gates`), `Build Core`, `Build Docs`, `Build UI Deps`, `Build & E2E UI`, `Live E2E UI`, `Test Core` 1–3 and 5–8, `Test UI` 2–16, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, both `PR-body guards`, one `Check Changeset`, and `Spec property liveness`.
  - **9 were skipped** (opt-in or path-filtered).
  - **3 are in progress:** `Test Core (4/8)`, `Test UI (1/16)`, and a second `Check Changeset` run.
  - **None has failed.**

### ④ Design judgment

**`skills/objectstack-data/SKILL.md`: holds.** The delta does not touch this file, and every judgment from `22db7aee` stands on the tree.
- I checked a verbatim copy of `defineObjectExtension({ extend: 'crm_account', fieldPatches: { industry: { label: 'Sector' }, type: { options: { customer: { label: 'Client' } } } } })` against HotCRM `main` `6961ab1`. `industry` (L311–318) is picklist-bound and the patch carries no `options`. `type` (L300–309) declares its own `options`, and L305 stores `customer`. `fieldPatchTargetMisses` returns `[]`, and `patchedField` applies both patches.
- `extend: 'crm_account'` and `label: 'Sector'` are whole tokens on L364, as eval cases 5 and 7 need.
- **Ratchet payment: no fact is lost.** Each fact of the deleted clause "; a base field changes only through `fieldPatches`" survives in the same file:
  - the channel is `fieldPatches`: L355;
  - the change is display-only: L356–360;
  - no other channel exists: `fields` is ruled out at L355–357, and in a `.custom` extension it is refused through the unsuffixed-field rule at L370–371; `overrides` is ruled out at L368; removal is ruled out at L349.

**`packages/spec/src/data/object.zod.ts`: does not hold.**
- **S2 from `22db7aee`: the scoping is resolved, but the new sentence is not true.** The comment no longer states `crm_account` facts as if they belonged to the example's `contact` target; it scopes them to "as on HotCRM's `crm_account`". That part is right.
- **M1 (must-fix).** L5133–5134 now read: "Where `industry` is picklist-bound, as on HotCRM's `crm_account`, only its **label is patchable**; an option patch goes on a field declaring its own options." That is a false rule.
  - A picklist binding blocks only the `options` part of a patch. `fieldPatchTargetMisses` judges `picklist` only inside the `options` loop (L110–127). `patchedField` applies every `BASE_FIELD_DISPLAY_WHITELIST.field` key (`label`, `description`, `inlineHelpText`, `placeholder`; field-customization.ts L77) whatever the binding, at registry.ts L643–647. Only the `options` branch checks `!picklistBound`.
  - The same file contradicts the comment 16 lines above it. The `fieldPatchesDescription()` example (L5117) patches `industry`'s `inlineHelpText` beside its `label`. The docs page `object-extensions.mdx` patches `industry`'s `inlineHelpText` too.
  - An author who reads the published `.d.ts` learns that HotCRM's `industry` takes nothing but a label. This card exists because one taught fact about this patch was wrong, and the delta adds another.
  - The fix is a few words on L5133–5134, e.g. "Where `industry` is picklist-bound, as on HotCRM's `crm_account`, its options are not patchable (its display keys are); an option patch goes on a field declaring its own options". The code block, the description and the changesets can stay as they are, and the fix needs no changeset change.
- The rest of the file holds as recorded on `22db7aee`. The description's new sentence is true of the code. A verbatim copy of the description example (`industry`: `label` plus `inlineHelpText`; `type`: `customer` option) under `extend: 'crm_account'` passes `fieldPatchTargetMisses` on HotCRM `main` with `[]`.

One must-fix (M1). S1 is resolved. S2 is resolved in scope, but its new wording is the must-fix.
